text:
Floating near the surface, six small eyes rise over the waves in search of feathered prey. With paddle-like limbs the large crustacean 
treads water with a slow measured pace to match the rhythm of the waves so as not to stir the water around the stalks of its peeking 
eyes. When a flock of sea birds approach, it will carefully raise its articulated maw from the water, retching out a mucus-covered stone 
shard, one of many that rest within its gullet. With all six eyes tracking the bird’s flight, a lethally precise hit cuts through the feathered 
prey, dropping it down to splash on the surface. With its prize floundering on the tide, the crustacean then awkwardly swims over to 
the dying bird and grasps it in its clawed forelimbs before it sinks and is lost to the many scavengers below the waves.
